title: Interpreting regulatory mechanisms of Hippo signaling through a deep learning sequence model.
authors: Dalal, Khyati; McAnany, Charles; Weilert, Melanie; McKinney, Mary Cathleen; Krueger, Sabrina; Zeitlinger, Julia
one_liner_zh: 该文用深度学习模型解析Hippo信号通路中TEAD4/YAP1与DNA结合的序列规则，并结合分子动力学模拟揭示TF-DNA协同结合机制，高度契合TF-DNA互作建模课题。
abstract: Signaling pathway components are well studied, but how they mediate cell-type-specific transcription responses is an unresolved problem. Using the Hippo pathway in mouse trophoblast stem cells as a model, we show that the DNA binding of signaling effectors is driven by cell-type-specific sequence rules that can be learned genome wide by deep learning models. Through model interpretation and experimental validation, we show that motifs for the cell-type-specific transcription factor TFAP2C enhance TEAD4/YAP1 binding in a nucleosome-range and distance-dependent manner, driving synergistic enhancer activation. We also discovered that Tead double motifs are widespread, highly active canonical response elements. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that TEAD4 binds them cooperatively through surprisingly labile protein-protein interactions that depend on the DNA template. These results show that the response to signaling pathways is encoded in the cis-regulatory sequences and that interpreting the rules reveals insights into the mechanisms by which signaling effectors influence cell-type-specific enhancer activity.
abstract_zh: 信号通路组分已被广泛研究，但它们如何介导细胞类型特异性转录反应仍是一个未解问题。以小鼠滋养层干细胞中的Hippo通路为模型，我们表明信号效应子的DNA结合由细胞类型特异性序列规则驱动，这些规则可通过深度学习模型在全基因组范围内学习。通过模型解释和实验验证，我们显示细胞类型特异性转录因子TFAP2C的基序以核小体范围和距离依赖性方式增强TEAD4/YAP1结合，驱动协同增强子激活。我们还发现Tead双基序广泛存在，是高度活跃的经典反应元件。分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟表明，TEAD4通过依赖于DNA模板的、令人惊讶地不稳定的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用协同结合这些基序。这些结果表明，对信号通路的反应编码在顺式调控序列中，而解读这些规则揭示了信号效应子影响细胞类型特异性增强子活性的机制见解。
